summary: Cherokee National Forest tower atop Buffalo Mountain near Unicoi, Tennessee: 1930 per the register, cab replaced by a covered platform in 2011, open to hikers year-round.

facts.design: 14x14 live-in wooden cab on a 40-ft steel tower with catwalk; cab replaced by a covered platform in 2011

access.note: The trail and the observation platform are open to visitors. The Forest Service lists the lookout as open year-round.

visit.trail_note: Hike or bike trail from the trailhead at Interstate 26 Exit 32 to the tower. No fees or permits. Horse and motorbike riding not allowed. The forest road FSR 188 is high-clearance, closed mid-January to mid-March, and ends at a gate about half a mile below the tower.

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Cherokee National Forest

events.note: Register gives 1930 as the build year. The trail wiki says the Civil Conservation Corps built it but gives no date.
Wiki says in service until 1989. Register says last staffed in the 1980s.
Registered May 10, 2005 on the National Historic Lookout Register as US 637, nominated by Nathan Coggins.
Register visit report: needs paint, first flight of stairs taken down, roof with at least one big hole, most glass out, steel in good shape, gate open.
Trail built by a contractor; the wiki says the 40-foot observation platform was restored as a joint partnership for $100,000.

Forest Service says the wood and metal structure was adapted to an all-metal covered viewing platform the same size as the old cab and catwalk. Register credits the Friends of Pinnacle Tower with the restoration, aided by an FFLA grant.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register gives 3,448 ft (1,051 m). Forest Service pages give 3,520 ft. The record keeps 1,051 m, the register figure.

The Forest Service hike page and the trail wiki give Interstate 26 Exit 32. The Forest Service lookout page gives Exit 32 in its access text and Exit 23 in its 'Hike or bike' line. The story uses Exit 32, the figure given by the hike page, the wiki and the lookout page's access text.
The Forest Service hike page gives the hike/bike trail as 4.9 and the lookout page as 5.9, with no unit. Not used in the story.
The register gives 1930 with no builder. The trail wiki credits the Civil Conservation Corps with no date. Not resolved from these sources.

notes_for_editor: Build date and builder are unresolved: the register says 1930 and the wiki credits the Civil Conservation Corps without a date. The CCC was set up in 1933 (not sourced here), so either the 1930 date or the builder credit needs checking against a Cherokee National Forest history or the Forest Service's own tower file. Access is public per the Forest Service pages, but the 2008 register visit is the only condition report; the 2011 restoration has no later condition report. The NHLR text about restoration is undated, so the story relies on the Forest Service date for 2011.
